chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ismail ibn Hammam said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not pelt the Jamarah on the day of the sacrifice until the sun rises.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'You should pelt the Jamarat from the middle of the valley, and place each Jamarah to your right. Then turn to the other side when you pelt the Jamarat Al-Aqabah.'

key_terms.الْجَمْرَة: The stone pillar or small pillar used in the stoning ritual of Hajj
key_terms.بَطْنُ الْوَادِي: The middle or belly of the valley (referring to the location of stoning)
key_terms.تَنْفَتِلُ: To turn or shift one's position/direction
key_terms.جَمْرَةَ الْعَقَبَةِ: The first and largest of the three pillars, specifically the one stoned on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the correct methods and timings for pelting the Jamarah during Hajj according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides precise jurisprudential details for the stoning of the Jamarah, emphasizing that the ritual on the Day of Sacrifice must commence only after the sun has fully risen to ensure the validity of the timing. The narration further instructs pilgrims to perform the stoning from the valley floor, positioning the pillar to the right, which reflects the traditional practice of facing the Kaaba while moving laterally, thereby integrating physical orientation with spiritual devotion.
